etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English tin, from Old English tin, from Proto-West Germanic *tin, from Proto-Germanic *tiną.

definitions.definition: (uncountable) A malleable, ductile, metallic element, resistant to corrosion, with atomic number 50 and symbol Sn.
(New Zealand, Australia, South Africa, Ireland, British, countable) An airtight container, made of tin or another metal, used to preserve food, or hold a liquid or some other product.

quote.citation: 1943 November and December, G. T. Porter, “The Lines Behind the Lines in Burma”, in Railway Magazine, page 325:
quote.text: When it arrived, the train was headed by a "K" class 4-6-0 wood-burning locomotive, and a water-tank wagon next to the tender was immediately besieged by women and girls, clad in their picturesque national costume, all with empty kerosene tins for water, a scene which was re-enacted at each stop down the line.

definitions.definition: (countable) A metal pan used for baking, roasting, storing food, etc.

quote.citation: 2023 October 28, “Next generation ‘clasico’: Bellingham faces 1st game against a Barcelona brimming with young talents”, in The Washington Times‎[1]:
quote.text: And, indeed, after a tense round of rolling, shaping and filling delicate pastry dough, Rowan can’t even pull his overstuffed pies out of the tins without them bleeding and oozing fruit filling.

quote.citation: 2023 April 30, “The Lions missed their chance, and the Eagles are smarter than everybody”, in The Washington Times‎[2]:
quote.text: Jones was insanely productive last season. He is a clinical route-runner who can line up at any position and catches everything.

definitions.definition: (countable, squash) The bottom part of the front wall, which is "out" if a player strikes it with the ball.
(slang, dated, uncountable) money, especially silver money.

quote.text: The father is a cotton lord, and they all have loads of tin, you know

quote.citation: 1861, Philip William Perfitt, The Pathfinder, page 377:
quote.text: When all your tin is gone and spent, / And you've not a mag for bread or rent

definitions.definition: Made of galvanised iron or built of corrugated iron.

quote.citation: 1939, George Orwell, Coming up for Air, London: Victor Gollancz:
quote.text: [I]n fact he was a big noise, literally, in the Baptist Chapel, known locally as the Tin Tab[ernacle] - whereas my family were 'church' and Uncle Ezekiel was an infidel at that.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To place into a metal can (ie. a tin; be it tin, steel, aluminum) in order to preserve.
To coat with solder, in preparation for soldering, to ensure a good solder joint
To coat with solder, in order to consolidate braided wire, so as to make contact with all strands and reduce fragility of the fraying wire
